A length pigeonhole argument gives both expansion and contraction of an optimal factorization when n>p(p-1), hence eventual equality. Two-run words attain p-1; verification.py rechecks 1,030 primitive cases and 741 two-run instances. Finite checks do not substitute for the universal proof.

value.rationale: The 2026 density paper leaves ordinary-limit behavior unasserted. For the natural entire family of periodic words with infinitely many palindrome prefixes, the result supplies a uniform effective decision bound, computes exact integer limits, and gives a period-sharp upper envelope attained for every p. The result is structurally motivated and not an arbitrary finite census.
